discovery: Development of massively parallel next-generation DNA sequencing (sequencing by synthesis)
rationale: Sequencing by synthesis is a chemical method: it uses reversible-terminator nucleotides, fluorescent labelling and cluster amplification on surfaces. It cut the cost of genome sequencing by orders of magnitude and changed biology and medicine. The work has already won major precursor prizes, including the Breakthrough Prize and the Millennium Technology Prize. Recent Chemistry prizes went to MOFs, AlphaFold/protein design, quantum dots and click chemistry, so this field has not been covered yet and is widely seen as overdue. The prize also tends to go to chemistry with a big impact on the life sciences.
